oncall-bot: [ALERT] spike of Xid 13 / ECC messages on inference-prod-us-west-2; kernel OOMs and container restarts observed across gpu-pool-6. Alert rate: 120/min. Creating incident INC-2026-581
Maya: I'm on it. seeing 5xx rate for text-generation route up ~18% and p95 latency up from 120ms to 1.2s :grimacing:
Sam R.: which node groups? any pattern by driver version or instance type?
Maya: mostly g4dn-type and p4d-suffix; driver 525.89 and node-kernel 5.15. Logs show Xid 13 errors then nv-hostengine restarts
Darren: paste some logs
Maya: ```
kubectl -n inference-prod logs gpu-inference-42 -c runtime
E0315 21:03:12.345 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00:00): 13, pid=4321, GPU 0: 0x86b0a2
E0315 21:03:12.347 containerd: runtime: failed to allocate memory for kv cache
OOMKilled
``` 
Carina: that's consistent with ECC parity errors -> elevated Xid 13. Could be hardware/dongle or a driver regression. Any recent node_reboots or kernel updates?
Maya: we rolled driver to 525.89 two days ago as part of scheduler rollout.
Sam R.: mitigation plan: 1) cordon and drain most noisy nodes 2) shift routing to fallback model-variant (cpu/quantized) 3) increase replica headroom on dedicated pool 4) contact infra vendor
Maya: cordoning noisy nodes now. running: kubectl cordon gpu-node-117 && kubectl drain gpu-node-117 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
opsbot: drain started on gpu-node-117 (pods evicted: 12)
Maya: updating routing policy to fallback-quantized for text-generation route
opsbot: routing config update applied: route=text-gen -> variant=fallback-quantized (drain in progress)
Sam R.: rolling restart of the driver safer? can we roll back to 520.xx? Vendor support recommended 520.56 for these SKUs earlier.
infra-vendor-bot: Vendor ticket #VEND-889 created; requested logs and node hardware run. ETA vendor engineer 30m.
Darren: for immediate relief, let's increase autoscaler target for dedicated-capacity by +30% and enable burst capacity
Maya: bumping dedicated pool min replicas
opsbot: dedicated pool scaled from 8 -> 11 replicas
jess: customer impact: page noise on support channel. Two customers reported 502s from inference API; estimate affected requests ~0.6% of total today but concentrated during spike windows
pm-anna: any customer-facing mitigation? throttling or circuit-breaker to reduce retries?
Sam R.: enabling per-customer rate limit on the high-volume tenants that are retrying aggressively. Also setting k8s eviction policy to prefer restart-delay for runtime containers to avoid tight crashloops
Maya: vendor sent back guidance: run nvidia-smi -q and check ECC flags, and if ECC parity errors present, isolate nodes. Advises not to roll driver in mid-incident without hardware confirmation
Maya: ran nvidia-smi -q on gpu-node-117: shows ECC CRC errors increasing on GPU0
Carina: plan: keep cordoned nodes powering down for maintenance, failover traffic, and if vendor confirms, schedule hardware replacement. Meanwhile route more traffic to lower-cost variants and enable cache warmup
Maya: started cache-warmup for fallback models to reduce cold-start latency
Sam R.: also added a temporary K8s taint to prevent new gpu jobs landing on remaining at-risk nodes: kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-11 stable=at-risk:NoSchedule
opsbot: taint applied to 4 nodes
Maya: monitoring metrics: Xid event rate falling slowly from 120/min to 30/min after drain, 5xx rate down to 6% now
Darren: progressing, but still see occasional driver resets on two nodes; vendor investigating hardware serials
infra-vendor-bot: vendor engineer connected, suggested collecting system vmcore and pci logs; uploaded to VEND-889
jess: support update drafted: "We observed transient GPU driver resets impacting some inference requests in us-west-2. We've rerouted traffic to fallback variants and are working with vendor for hardware validation. Some customers saw increased latency/5xx; mitigation in progress." Ready to send once we stabilize
Maya: preparing postmortem notes and will capture key timelines. Creating incident record INC-2026-581 with mitigation steps
Sam R.: next steps: after vendor confirms hardware, schedule node replacement, and consider pinning driver to 520.56 on a canary subset; add regression detection test to CI for driver 525.x
Carina: noting operational learning: add automated routing fallback to quantized variant on GPU node flaps, with circuit-breaker to limit throughput to affected pools
pm-anna: ask CS to reach out to top-affected customers proactively with ETA
Maya: handing off to night oncall Lee in 30m. Lee, summary: cordoned 5 nodes, drained 3, dedicated pool scaled +3, routing -> fallback-quantized, vendor engaged VEND-889, still occasional resets but customer impact reduced
Lee: taking over, will watch for recurring Xid spikes and validate vendor remediation. Thanks
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-581 transitioned to oncall Lee. Handoff notes captured.
Maya: adding final log snippet for root cause analysis:
```
Kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00:00): 13, PID 8743, GPU 0: 0x86b12e - ECC parity error, resetting GPU
Container runtime: runtime: container killed due to OOM after nv-hostengine crash
``` 
Maya: closing slack thread for now, will update postmortem when vendor confirms hardware findings. :white_check_mark:
